headline: Bank of England Proposes Cut to U.K. Bank Capital Requirements

paragraphs.text: Capital requirements on major U.K. banks could be lowered under proposals from the Bank of England, releasing more capital to be used on dividends, buybacks or lending.
The Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee on Thursday said it has completed a review of the framework that dictates how much capital U.K. banks are required to hold.
The proposed changes would reduce Tier 1 capital requirements for major U.K. banks by around 50 basis points of risk-weighted assets in normal times.
The measures will free up more capacity to lend to U.K. households and businesses, the BOE said. The actual impact of the proposals will vary depending on the banks' business models.

As part of the reforms, the U.K. Prudential Regulation Authority will consider lower minimum requirements for domestic lending to offset the buffer provided by maintaining a 2% neutral countercyclical capital buffer rate.
This will also better reflect the risks of geographic concentration of lending, the central bank said.
The BOE said the reforms would make capital requirements more proportionate and better targeted.

The reduction would mean system-wide risk-weighted Tier 1 requirements for major U.K. banks would be in line with the committee's updated benchmark of around 13%, which was reduced from around 14% last year.
Lowering capital requirements much further would put financial stability and sustainable economic growth at risk, the BOE warned.
A further cut to capital needs could cause banks to lose market confidence more quickly in the case of losses, pushing up borrowing costs for households and businesses.

Following the completion of the review, the Financial Policy Committee and the PRA will consult on the reforms, and aim to implement them as soon as possible. Further consultations will take place in the first half of 2027.
